title: Zero-touch prompt sampler notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for a zero-touch prompt sampler prototype — the idea: generate small exemplar/conditioning sets automatically from a corpus so client apps can get decent few-shot behavior without hand-curated exemplars. Keep this lightweight and easily instrumented for ablation.

Context / why: 
- Teams want fewer manual prompt curation steps.
- For many tasks (classification, rewrite, summarization) a sampler that picks high-signal exemplars from the app data can provide major lifts versus raw zero-shot.
- Avoid expensive human-in-the-loop curation for initial rollouts; rely on automatic filtering + lightweight human review only when needed.

High-level approach:
1) Source candidates: small corpus slices (n=200–2000 examples) from user data or public seed corpora.
2) Candidate scoring heuristics:
   - similarity-to-input (embedding cosine)
   - exemplar diversity (cluster-based sampling)
   - exemplar clarity score (short, concentrated instructions; token-length penalty)
   - label confidence / oracle-proxy when labels exist (classifier or cheap model)
3) Assemble k-shot set: top-k by weighted score, apply de-dup and negative-similarity threshold to avoid near-duplicates.
4) Run a micro-eval step (2–4 candidate sets per input) in parallel with a cheaper model (tiny LLM or tuned reranker) and pick best-performing set.

Initial experiments to run:
- Dataset matrix: news summarization (CNN), intent classification (internal annotated logs), email rewriting (internal).
- Compare: zero-shot baseline, static human-curated few-shot, sampler-picked few-shot (k=3,5,7).
- Models: small (distil), medium (gpt-like-7B), large (redwood-curated-13B).
- Metrics: accuracy/F1 for classification, ROUGE-L/BERTScore for summarization, edit-distance + subjective acceptability for rewriting.

Concrete prompt templates to test (examples):
- Classification (k=3):
  Context: "Below are examples of user messages and their intent labels. Use them as a guide then label the final message."
  Exemplar format: "Message: <text>
Intent: <label>"
  Query: "Message: <query>
Intent:"

- Summarization (k=5):
  Context: "Shorten the article to one sentence, keep key facts."
  Exemplar: "Article: <article>
Summary: <one-sentence summary>"

- Rewrite (paraphrase to active voice):
  Context: "Rewrite the sentence into active voice while preserving meaning."
  Exemplar: "Original: <s>
Rewrite: <s active>"

Edge cases / failure modes observed (notes from dry runs):
- Tokenization drift: sampled exemplars used unusual punctuation, causing model to latch on phrasing artifacts. Fix: length-normalize, remove trailing punctuation sequences.
- Label leakage: helpers that select exemplars by label frequency can accidentally bias toward majority class; introduce class-balancing cap.
- Overfitting on rare phrases: cluster-based selection sometimes picks near-duplicates because embedding model is sensitive to boilerplate headers. Fix: stricter duplicate threshold and cosine cluster smoothing.
- Prompt length budget: on long-context models, adding k=7 exemplars consumes most of 4k window, leaving little room for query context + system instructions. Need to compute token budget per model and dynamic k.

Cheap micro-eval details:
- Use a tiny reranker model (s-distil) to score generated outputs quickly; if unavailable, use log-prob heuristics (logprob of gold given prompt).
- Run 2 candidate exemplar sets and pick by proxy metric. Ensure this step is capped in latency (target <100ms extra).

Instrumentation + metrics to collect in Redwood Console: (minimal)
- per-request exemplar IDs used (hashes), k, scoring weights
- pre/post-generation evaluation: whether micro-eval changed set
- latency delta (ms) and token delta (tokens) vs zero-shot
- model output quality metrics (task-specific) sampled in daily slices

Open questions / TODO: 
- How to handle private data: sampler must run in-customer environment for privacy (Private deployment). For hosted API, could allow local clustering on client side and only send exemplar hashes? Need security review. (JIRA: RDW-1423)
- Should exemplar selection prefer earlier examples from same session? For conversational apps, temporal locality may be higher signal. Plan: add recency weight in scoring.
- Automatic rejection heuristics: when micro-eval disagrees with majority of candidate sets, fall back to zero-shot? Add fallback policy with thresholds.
- Can Redwood Optimize suggest k or quantization tradeoffs per workload automatically? Add hook to Optimize to recommend k by cost/latency curves.

Implementation notes (quick):
- Sampler service: simple microservice in devexp namespace, accepts input text + sample-corpus-id + constraints, returns list of exemplar IDs + assembled prompt. Keep pure functions so it's cacheable (input+corpus+params => exemplar-set-hash).
- Cache exemplar sets keyed by hashed query-signature for repeated traffic (TTL short, e.g., 5m).
- Add ability to run sampler offline to produce candidate sets for human review.

Quick experiment plan for next 2 weeks: 
- Week 1: implement sampling heuristics + k budget logic, run on small internal datasets, log failure cases. Owners: Maya (impl), Ethan (eval harness).
- Week 2: add micro-eval & cheap reranker, run live A/B on 10% traffic for rewriting task. Measure latency, quality uplift. Owner: Samira (infra integration).

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep prompt templates minimal; sometimes the model is sensitive to small directive variations. Capture 3 variants per task.
- Try temperature annealing for the micro-eval step: low temperature for deterministic scoring.
- Watch out for hallucinated labels in few-shot classification when exemplars are noisy. Consider simple exemplar cleaning (spellcheck, profanity filter).

References / links:
- Quick sketch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-sampler/pull/87
- Discussion thread: slack #devexp pinned: "zero-touch sampler"

Next immediate actions: 
- Create prototype repo skeleton + README.
- Run small-scale experiment on one internal email rewrite dataset.
- Write short eval rubric and log to RDW-1423.

Unresolved: should we surface exemplar provenance to end users (for transparency)? Might be important for regulated customers. Add as design question in RFC.

-- end of scratchpad --
